audit_methodology: Each case classified by comparing actual cumulative likes/reports signal vs expected verdict. Algorithm's job is to judge OBSERVED user signal, not infer hidden quality. Test cases where simulator produced positive signal (likes >> reports) but expects 'sunk' = TEST_BUG (over-strict expectation). Test cases where simulator produced negative signal but algorithm judged alive = ALGO_BUG. 1:1 ratios near boundary = EDGE_CASE. stable_bad / stable_good arcs producing signal opposite to their named quality = CALIBRATION.

stable_bad.note: Most stable_bad failures: simulator produced likes >= reports (often likes > reports) yet test expected sunk. Algorithm correctly read positive signal. CALIBRATION items are quality=0.10 simulator runs that produced strongly positive ratios (e.g. 17L/6R, 23L/13R).

controversial_persistent.note: ALL 28 cases: likes > reports (often 2:1 or 3:1). Algorithm correctly judged healthy. Test expectation 'sunk_or_borderline' is wrong — controversial mark with majority positive votes IS healthy by user signal.

collapse.note: Algorithm correctly reads cumulative positive signal. 'Collapse' is a temporal pattern the chaos-monkey expects but cumulative likes/reports don't reflect it. Algorithm cannot detect decay if cumulative ratio is still positive — this is by design (signal-based, not quality-inferring).

doc_stale.note: Same as collapse — temporal decay invisible in cumulative signal.

seasonal.note: Mixed. context_dependent expectation is itself ambiguous — counted clearly positive cumulative as TEST_BUG, clearly positive sunk by algo as ALGO_BUG.

short_burst.note: Burst already deposited likes; algorithm correctly preserves them. Expected 'sunk' is over-strict given cumulative positive ratio.

stable_good.note: ALGO_BUG: high cumulative positive ratio (e.g. 937L/284R, 602L/292R, 374L/227R, 110L/72R) yet algorithm sunk. Algorithm is too aggressive in sinking — likely exposure-aging or report-recency over-weighting overpowers persistent positive cumulative.

recovery.note: Most 'recovery' failures: simulator never produced enough recovery likes (final state likes=0-2 vs reports=3-7). The mark really is bad in current data — TEST_BUG. Only one case where signal was clearly positive but sunk.

short_attack.note: Split: where final cumulative is negative, algorithm is right (TEST_BUG); where likes >> reports cumulatively (244L/91R, 205L/112R, 482L/219R), algorithm wrong (ALGO_BUG).

remote_silent.note: ALGO_BUG: 11L/3R, 16L/6R, 30L/9R, 25L/5R, 15L/5R sunk despite strongly positive ratio. Algorithm over-penalizes silence even when signal is positive. EDGE_CASE for cases with likes=0, reports=1-2 (algo correctly sinks weak negative, but expected alive due to remoteness — both defensible).

doc_official.note: ALGO_BUG: official content with positive cumulative (53L/49R, 29L/21R, 128L/104R) sunk. Algorithm should respect the strong positive signal from a verified source.

test_changes: controversial_persistent: change expected from 'sunk_or_borderline' to 'context_dependent' or 'alive_if_likes_dominate'. The arc by definition has strong likes AND strong reports — majority positive should mean alive.

collapse / doc_stale: cumulative-signal algorithm cannot detect decay. Either (a) test expected should be 'alive_if_cumulative_positive', or (b) simulator needs to model report acceleration in late phase strongly enough that cumulative ratio inverts. Currently simulator produces e.g. 242L/60R for 'collapse' which is not a collapse at all.

stable_bad: when quality=0.10 simulator produces likes >= reports, the case is mis-calibrated. Either tighten simulator (likes should be rare for bad marks) or relax expected to 'sunk_or_borderline_or_weak'.

short_burst: change expected from 'sunk' to 'sunk_or_alive_with_decay' since cumulative likes from the burst legitimately persist. Or have simulator actively decay cumulative weight in the silent tail.
seasonal context_dependent: remove this expectation entirely or make it 'no_judgment' — context-dependent is not a testable expectation.
recovery: when simulator produces final-state likes < reports (e.g. 0L/3R), the arc didn't actually recover — these should expect 'sunk', not 'alive'. Filter or fix.
remote_silent with positive likes (>= 2 likes per report): expected 'alive' is correct — keep as is, this is an algo bug not a test bug.
algo_changes: stable_good cluster (14/14 ALGO_BUG, 100%): Algorithm is sinking high-quality marks with 2-3:1 positive cumulative ratios over long time spans. Likely cause: exposure aging or capital-decay term over-penalizing total exposure even when ratio stays positive. Consider: floor life at 0 if cumulative likes/reports ratio > 1.5 over project lifetime.

remote_silent (9/13 ALGO_BUG, 69%): Algorithm penalizes long silence even when prior signal is strongly positive. Consider: silence should reduce confidence/exposure but not actively decay positive signal capital below zero.

short_attack (6/12 ALGO_BUG, 50%): Algorithm overweights recent reports relative to long-run cumulative. Consider: recency window should not exceed e.g. 30 days for sinking decisions when cumulative ratio is strongly positive.
doc_official (4/5 ALGO_BUG, 80%): Official-source marks getting sunk with positive ratios. Algorithm needs source-priority awareness or simply respect cumulative signal.
recommendations.priority: FIX TEST FIRST. 132/207 = 64% of failures are test set bugs (over-strict expectations or impossible-to-detect temporal patterns). After fixing test, real algorithm pass rate will jump substantially. Then address the 38 ALGO_BUGs which cluster in stable_good + remote_silent + doc_official + short_attack — all share the pattern of 'long history with positive cumulative ratio being sunk anyway', suggesting one shared root cause (exposure aging or recency overweight) in the algorithm.
